record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: Determine whether results obtained from applying algebraic analysis to the Moisil-Theodoresco system can be used to obtain information about the Cauchy-Fueter system.

evidence.quote: Problem: Is it possible to use these results to get information on the Cauchy-Fueter system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with coordinates $(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)$. The (left) Cauchy–Fueter operator acting on quaternion-valued functions $f = f_0 + f_1 i + f_2 j + f_3 k$ is
$$D_{CF} f \;=\; \partial_{x_0} f + i\,\partial_{x_1} f + j\,\partial_{x_2} f + k\,\partial_{x_3} f,$$
and a function is (left) Fueter regular when $D_{CF}f=0$. In several quaternionic variables $q^{(1)},\dots,q^{(n)} \in \mathbb{H}$, the Cauchy–Fueter system is the overdetermined system $D^{(\ell)}_{CF} f = 0$ for $\ell=1,\dots,n$, where $D^{(\ell)}_{CF}$ is the Cauchy–Fueter operator in the $\ell$-th quaternionic variable.

The Moisil–Theodoresco system in $\mathbb{R}^3$ acts on functions $W:\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}\oplus \mathbb{R}^3$, $W = W_0 + W_1 e_1 + W_2 e_2 + W_3 e_3$, by
$$\partial W \;=\; \big(e_1\partial_{x_1} + e_2\partial_{x_2} + e_3\partial_{x_3}\big) W \;=\; 0,$$
equivalently $\operatorname{div}\vec W=0$ and $\operatorname{grad}W_0+\operatorname{curl}\vec W=0$. Its several-variables version is the overdetermined system obtained by imposing this Dirac-type equation in each of $n$ groups of three real variables.

By "algebraic analysis" of such an overdetermined system one means the study, via commutative algebra and $\mathcal{D}$-module techniques, of the associated module $M = \mathcal{R}^p/\mathcal{R}^q P$ over the polynomial ring $\mathcal{R} = \mathbb{C}[\xi]$ (or the corresponding ring of differential operators), including its syzygies, its free resolution, the cohomology of the resulting complex, the characteristic variety, and the resulting compatibility conditions, removable singularities theorems, Hartogs-type phenomena, and Ext-module obstructions.

Problem. Determine whether information obtained by applying algebraic analysis (free resolutions, syzygies, characteristic varieties, Ext-modules, and the associated cohomological invariants) to the Moisil–Theodoresco system in several variables can be transferred to yield analogous information about the Cauchy–Fueter system in several quaternionic variables. Concretely, exhibit either:
(a) a functorial/algebraic correspondence between the $\mathcal{R}$-modules associated to the two systems that transports free resolutions and Ext-modules from one to the other, together with the resulting analytic consequences (e.g. removable singularities, Hartogs phenomena, structure of compatibility conditions) for Cauchy–Fueter; or
(b) an obstruction proving that no such transfer is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search returns the problem-listing source and surrounding work on Clifford/quaternionic analysis (Abreu Blaya et al. on generalized Moisil–Théodoresco systems; surveys on quaternionic analysis as a special case of Clifford analysis in $\mathbb{R}^4$). These works establish structural links between the two systems but do not announce a definitive answer to whether algebraic-analysis results on Moisil–Theodoresco transfer to Cauchy–Fueter in several variables. No publication was found that explicitly resolves the question, so the status is best recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems on the Analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter System in Several Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Listing of open problems concerning algebraic analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in the listed source.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Moisil-Théodoresco Systems and Cauchy Integral Decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: Defines generalized Moisil-Théodoresco systems and proves structure theorems and Cauchy integral decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: Related structural results on Moisil-Théodoresco systems exist but do not transfer algebraic-analysis information to Cauchy-Fueter in several variables.

status_evidence.title: Quaternionic Analysis and Some Conventional Theories
status_evidence.snippet: Quaternionic analysis viewed as solutions to a generalized Moisil-Théodoresco system in R^4.
status_evidence.claim: Connections between the systems are known but the algebraic-analysis transfer question is not resolved.
